A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PLEIADES. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained content can be reliably matched across layout changes.

before.justification: V4 reports original DVS128 classification, 3ET+ eye-tracking and Prophesee GEN4 detection results, alongside appendix sparsity measurements and ablations.

after.justification: V5 retains those original results and adds PLEIADES results on KITTI 2D object detection in Appendix B.3.

M1.justification: The polynomial kernel construction, discretization, contraction optimization and network components are unchanged. Appendix B.3 explicitly reuses the existing GEN4 architecture for KITTI; no changed algorithm or architectural adaptation is documented.

E1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds KITTI 2D object detection on conventional-camera recordings. This extends evaluation beyond event-camera inputs to a distinct input modality, while retaining DVS128, 3ET+ and GEN4.

E2.justification: New Table 9 adds reported comparisons with RGBD Fusion (YOLOv2) and SimCLR (ResNet50). Comparator membership in the existing benchmark comparisons remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The new KITTI comparison specifies a 10 FPS assumption for calculating MACs per second and uses the Table 8 detector. Existing experiments retain their settings and metrics. KITTI-specific splits and training budgets are not documented.

E4.justification: Figure 3's latency, masking and resampling analyses, Table 5's quantized-network sparsity measurements, and Tables 6–7's polynomial-degree and Jacobi-parameter ablations are retained unchanged. KITTI supplies additional benchmark results rather than a new ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: The statements about 25 trials and mean/standard-error reporting, with the Prophesee exception, remain unchanged. Table 9 provides point estimates without additional run counts, uncertainty estimates or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Table 9 adds KITTI mAP values of 0.576 for PLEIADES, 0.570 for SimCLR and 0.482 for RGBD Fusion. PLEIADES is reported with 0.57 M parameters and 18 B MACs/sec at 10 FPS. These are additional task-specific results; all numerical rows in Tables 1–8 and Figure 3's curves are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), Appendix A's contraction arguments and the memory/compute expressions are unchanged. The added Jacobi discussion provides informal motivation and explicitly leaves a mathematical justification of training dynamics outside the paper's scope.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same claims about polynomial temporal kernels, efficiency, event-based benchmark performance and resampling without fine-tuning. KITTI adds support for conventional-camera applicability already claimed in v4.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly explains Jacobi-parameter effects through training dynamics rather than expressivity and motivates -0.25 as a Legendre/Chebyshev compromise. It acknowledges the absence of a full theoretical justification. One sentence inconsistently specifies +0.25, although the stated setting and Table 7 retain -0.25. Section 6's limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: The introduction adds a repository access pointer for structured-kernel code and a pretrained DVS128 model. Appendix B.3 identifies reuse of the Table 8 architecture. Existing implementation, hyperparameter, hardware and training-time disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: V5 adds Pei et al. (2025), Optimized real-time speech enhancement with deep SSMs on raw audio, to the contraction discussion and references. Section 4 also more explicitly attributes ancillary design choices to Pei et al. (2024). The broader related-work positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized additions comprise the introductory KITTI and code disclosures, the Section 4 rationale, and Appendix B.3. The publication footer changes to NeurIPS 2025. Most prose and the section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: V5 adds Table 9 and adjusts pagination and table placement. Tables 6–7 appear alongside their ablation discussion, and Table 8 shares a page with the GEN4 details. Figures 1–3 retain identical graphics; existing table contents and structures are preserved.

improvement.justification: The code and pretrained-model access information improves reproducibility guidance, while KITTI adds preliminary evidence for conventional-camera applicability. These gains are limited by unspecified KITTI splits and baseline provenance, plus the sign inconsistency in the new Jacobi rationale. The established empirical and theoretical content is preserved.
